body:
### v18.19.0 optimization decision

The contained `holotreeBenchmark` task produces a reproducible five-run many-small-file baseline with wall/CPU time, bytes, file counts, source context, and raw JSON. That baseline is insufficient to justify changing storage or materialization.

**v18.19 decision: no storage/materializer optimization is selected.** zstd, packfiles, FUSE, reflinks/hardlinks, and related format changes remain outside v18.19.

The representative RCC-native workload matrix, native-platform measurements, pprof/syscall evidence, and external Actions workload requested by the full issue are not complete. This issue stays open; the current synthetic baseline is not presented as full acceptance.

### Scope correction — full RCC program required

The earlier v18.19 disposition comment that placed required acceptance outside the release is superseded.

Every RCC-owned required acceptance criterion in this issue remains part of the v18.19.0 completion graph. It must be implemented and recorded as **PASS** with exact code, test/runtime evidence, and SHA before #120 can release. No `PARTIAL`, `FUTURE`, or `DEFERRED` result is acceptable for required RCC-owned acceptance.

Explicit issue non-goals and conditional experiments remain non-goals/conditional; this correction does not require Kubernetes, a broker, shared writable fleet Holotree, mandatory OCI/FUSE/zstd/packfiles/reflinks, a TUI, downstream implementation, replacement of `rccremote`, or an embeddable-Go-library rewrite.

PR #119 must not merge and no RC/stable tag may be published until this issue's full accepted RCC scope passes.

### Scope correction — optimization research no longer blocks v18.19.0

This comment supersedes this issue's earlier v18.19 scope-correction and performance-completion comments **for #125 only**.

The Environment Artifact architecture does not depend on selecting a new physical storage/materialization implementation. PR #119 already establishes the durable boundary we need: cryptographic Environment Artifact identity, provider-backed publication/acquisition, verification, worker-local materialization, leases, and execution remain independent of the physical Holotree storage/materializer implementation.

For **v18.19.0**, the supported implementation may therefore ship with the current proven **v12 gzip/object-per-file Holotree materializer/storage path** behind the new Environment Artifact lifecycle. v18.19 does **not** require zstd, packfiles, FUSE/lazy materialization, reflink/clonefile, compressed filesystem images/COW overlays, or any other replacement materializer before release.

The six-way comparative optimization program remains valid work in this issue, but it is now **post-v18.19 performance R&D rather than a release gate**. This issue should remain open after v18.19 unless its full benchmark/recommendation contract is actually completed. Deferring that research does not imply that any candidate was rejected or that the current gzip/object-per-file implementation is permanently preferred.

### v18.19 release boundary

Before v18.19 may release:

- the current materializer/storage path must continue to satisfy the Environment Artifact correctness, compatibility, verification, lease, crash/repair, archive/provider, and rollback gates owned by the other release-blocking issues;
- existing benchmark evidence may be retained as a truthful baseline/regression aid;
- release notes must not claim unproven storage/materialization performance improvements;
- no optimization-format change should be added opportunistically to PR #119 solely to close #125.

The full #125 research remains responsible for later determining, with representative native evidence, whether gzip/object-per-file, zstd, hybrid packfiles, reflink/clonefile, lazy/virtual materialization, filesystem-image/COW, or another evidence-backed approach should become a future platform default.

### Program consequence

#125 is no longer part of the **blocking v18.19.0 completion set**. #120/PR #119 should reconcile their completion contract accordingly: release readiness is determined by the remaining Environment Artifact correctness/compatibility/security/provider/archive/coordination gates plus the contained RC/release lane, not by completion of this optimization search.
